subtopics.title: Plot line, domain and range
subtopics.exposition: The domain of a straight line function is all real numbers, {x : x in R}, because there is no value of x for which f(x) is undefined. The range of f(x) = mx + c is all real numbers, because f(x) can take on any real value. To complete a table of values for a function, substitute each given value of x into the equation to find the corresponding f(x). Plot the points from the table and join them with a straight line to draw the graph. Each pair (x, f(x)) from the table gives a point to plot, and points are written with a semicolon between the coordinates, for example (-2, -2) and (0, 0).

subtopics.title: Gradient, y-intercept and equation
subtopics.exposition: Functions of the form y = mx + c are called straight line functions. In y = mx + c, m and c are constants, and they have different effects on the graph of the function. The standard form of a straight line graph is the equation y = mx + c. m is referred to as the gradient of a straight-line graph. c is known as the y-intercept. As m increases, the gradient of the graph increases. The value of c affects where the graph cuts the y-axis. If c > 0, the graph shifts vertically upwards. If c < 0, the graph shifts vertically downwards.

subtopics.title: Intercepts and dual intercept method
subtopics.exposition: If m > 0, the graph increases from left to right (the graph slopes upwards). If m < 0, the graph slopes downwards. Every point on the y-axis has an x-coordinate of 0. Every point on the x-axis has a y-coordinate of 0. To sketch a graph of the form f(x) = mx + c, three characteristics must be determined. Only two points are needed to plot a straight line graph. Always write the function in the form y = mx + c and take note of m before sketching. To calculate the y-intercept, let x = 0. To calculate the x-intercept, let y = 0. For g(x) = x - 1, letting x = 0 gives g(0) = -1, so the y-intercept is the point (0, -1). For g(x) = x - 1, letting y = 0 gives x = 1, so the x-intercept is the point (1, 0). The three characteristics needed to sketch f(x) = mx + c are the sign of m, the y-intercept and the x-intercept. In the dual intercept method, the two points used are the x-intercept and the y-intercept, as these are the easiest points to use. Dual intercept method, step 1: examine the standard form of the equation to find the sign of m, which tells whether the graph increases or decreases. Dual intercept method, step 2: calculate the intercepts, letting x = 0 for the y-intercept and y = 0 for the x-intercept. Dual intercept method, step 3: plot the two intercept points and draw the graph.

subtopics.title: Sketch by gradient-intercept method
subtopics.exposition: The gradient of a line is the measure of steepness. Steepness is determined by the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change. The gradient m equals the change in y divided by the change in x, that is, the vertical change over the horizontal change. A straight line graph y = mx + c can be drawn using the gradient (m) and the y-intercept (c). In the gradient-intercept method, calculate the y-intercept by letting x = 0; this gives the first point (0, c). In the gradient-intercept method, the gradient is used to calculate the second point. The same gradient can be written as a change up and to the right, or as the matching change down and to the left; for example 3 up over 2 right equals 3 down over 2 left. Gradient-intercept method, step 1: use the intercept. For p(x) = (1/2)x - 3, c = -3, which gives the point (0, -3). Gradient-intercept method, step 2: use the gradient. For m = 1/2, start at (0, -3) and move 1 unit up and 2 units to the right to get the second point (2, -2). Alternatively, from (0, -3) move 1 unit down and 2 units to the left to get the second point (-2, -4). Gradient-intercept method, step 3: plot the two points and draw the graph.
